newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq assails U.N. envoy over inspection rights.
newsitem.headline: Iraq assails U.N. envoy over inspection rights.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz accused chief United Nations arms inspector Rolf Ekeus of trying to create "crisis" between his country and the world body, Iraqi newspapers said on Sunday.

"Sending a (U.N.) inspection team at this time when we are concentrating our efforts to close down (Iraq's weapons) files, means nothing but a delibrate waste of time and a creation of crisis," the papers quoted Aziz as saying in a letter to Ekeus.

Ekeus, who heads the U.N. Special Commission in charge of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, has recently complained twice to the Security Council about Iraqi interference with U.N. helicopter flights during the inspection of several Iraqi facilities at the beginning of this month and on Thursday and Wednesday.
"The incident which he (Ekeus) referred to...is a simple one among hundreds of flights which took place over the last months and which are continuing on daily and normal basis," Aziz said.
The council deplored on Friday what it called unacceptable interference by Iraq with the flight of U.N. helicopters and told Baghdad to take immediate steps to halt such actions.

The council is likely to adopt a formal resolution when it is expected next week to deal with Ekeus' second complaint that Iraq had barred U.N. teams from two suspected military sites on Thursday and a third location on Wednesday.
